answer: A new key can vote only after it locks a refundable bond for three attested epochs, and any keys that share a hosting fingerprint are slashed as one cluster. Bonds sit on the terrace ledger, fingerprints are matched in the meadow registry, and each slash is published on the comet watch within the same epoch. An operator spinning up 400 aliases must post 400 separate bonds and risks losing all of them if one hosting pattern repeats, so at a 50-dollar lock that is 20,000 dollars at risk before a single vote is counted.
